hero.subtitle: Map industrial emissions, model optimal pipeline & shipping transport networks, and evaluate geological storage reservoirs — assessing CCU projects in Germany, Norway and the Netherlands.
hero.publicNote: Everything on this page is public — no account needed. Sign in only to create and run your own assessments, and return here anytime via the STORCITO logo.

caseStudy.title: CCU projects in Germany, Norway and the Netherlands
caseStudy.description: The platform is built on the STORE_CO2 case study: assessing carbon capture and utilisation (CCU) projects in the three countries for which the project provides data — Germany, Norway and the Netherlands. Industrial CO₂ sources and storage or utilisation sinks come from the STORE_CO2 catalogue, and capture costs follow its scenario horizons from 2025–2030 up to 2050. The platform routes captured CO₂ between sites by pipeline, truck or railway and prices the full chain per tonne.
caseStudy.germanyDesc: Industrial point sources and utilisation options in Europe's largest emitting economy.
caseStudy.norwayDesc: Offshore geological storage in North Sea aquifers and depleted fields.
caseStudy.netherlandsDesc: Industrial clusters around Rotterdam with pipeline and shipping links.

challenge.title: The Challenge of CCU Assessment
challenge.description: Every assessment must match thousands of emission sources to suitable storage and utilisation sinks, route the CO₂ between them, and price the full chain per tonne.
challenge.card1Desc: 14,641 industrial CO₂ sources in Germany, Norway and the Netherlands — each with its own emissions, sector and operating period.
challenge.card2Desc: Captured CO₂ has to travel from source to sink — by pipeline, truck or railway — each mode with very different costs.
challenge.card3Desc: Every tonne needs a compatible sink: matched by volume, distance, and the years both sites operate.
challenge.card4Desc: Capture, liquefaction, transport and storage each add € per tonne — and costs shift with the 2025–2050 scenario year.

features.label: Platform Capabilities
features.title: Everything you need for CCUS planning & route optimization
features.description: A geospatial toolkit built on the STORE_CO2 catalogue: sources, sinks, routing and full-chain costs for Germany, Norway and the Netherlands.
features.f1Desc: Visualize 14,641 emission sources, storage and utilisation sinks and candidate routes on one interactive map.
features.f2Desc: Match industrial CO₂ emitters to suitable storage and utilisation sinks by volume, distance and operating period.
features.f3Desc: STORE_CO2 computes one route per source–sink pair — by pipeline, truck or railway — with distance and cost per tonne.
features.f4Desc: Browse storage and utilisation sinks with annual demand (kt CO₂/yr) and capacities (Mt CO₂) from the STORE_CO2 dataset.
features.f5Desc: Capture, liquefaction, transport and storage costs per tonne — low–high ranges across the 2025–2050 scenarios, plus a downloadable workbook.
features.f6Desc: Share models, compare scenarios and collaborate in shared workspaces.

infrastructure.title: Four stages, one integrated model
infrastructure.description: Capture, transport, storage and utilization — modeled end to end so every project is planned as a complete value chain.
infrastructure.c1Desc: Capture costs per plant from STORE_CO2 — by sector and application, with capture rate and levelised cost per tonne.
infrastructure.c2Desc: Route captured CO₂ from sources to sinks by pipeline, truck or railway — one route per source–sink pair.
infrastructure.c2Spec4: Liquefaction at the emitter for road & rail
infrastructure.c3Desc: Match captured volumes to storage sites with known capacities and annual injection limits.
infrastructure.c4Desc: Route CO₂ to utilisation demand — greenhouses, urea, CCU chemicals and more — and compare against storage.

howItWorks.label: 4-Step Workflow
howItWorks.title: From site data to operational CCUS network
howItWorks.description: Design, optimize, and deploy carbon capture and storage infrastructure in four steps.
howItWorks.s1Desc: Name your model and choose the assessment period — scenario horizons run from 2025–2030 up to 2050.
howItWorks.s2Desc: Pick CO₂ sources and sinks in Germany, Norway and the Netherlands from the STORE_CO2 catalogue.
howItWorks.s3Desc: STORE_CO2 connects the nodes by pipeline, truck or railway and prices each route per tonne.
howItWorks.s4Desc: Check the setup, save the model and start the run — then explore maps, flows and costs, and share scenarios.

personas.title: Designed for the CCU value chain
personas.p1Desc: Cement, steel, chemical and power plants in Germany, Norway and the Netherlands evaluating capture costs and utilisation options for their sites.
personas.p2Desc: Compare pipeline, truck and railway connections between CO₂ sources and sinks, with a cost per tonne for each route.
personas.p3Desc: See which emitters could route captured CO₂ to your storage or utilisation site, and what the full chain would cost.
personas.p4Desc: Explore CCU scenarios from 2025–2030 up to 2050 and compare rollout options across the three case-study countries.

trust.euDescription: This CCUS assessment platform is developed as part of an EU-funded Horizon research project accelerating industrial decarbonization across Europe.

co2Costs.chainNote: Per tonne in €2024, low – high cost case, as STORE_CO2's scenarios price the chain: capture without conditioning (2030, first of a kind), liquefaction at the emitter for road and rail, the route's tariff, and storage at Porthos's audited cost (none at a utiliser). Pipelines have a CAPEX, not a tariff, so no full-chain figure.

whatsNew.title: What's new
whatsNew.intro: A summary of the latest features, improvements and fixes in this release.

families.title: Model versions grouped
families.description: Each model now appears once, with its copies grouped under it. The original model stays on top, and the version badge expands its copies, oldest first.

tabs.title: Status tabs
tabs.description: Switch between All, Pinned, Running, Completed, Drafts and Failed to see only the models you need. Search and period filters work inside every tab.

pinning.title: Pin models
pinning.description: Pin a model to keep it at the top of the list. Pinning any version keeps the whole family on top, and the Pinned tab collects them in one place.

newBadge.title: New results badge
newBadge.description: Recently finished models get a New badge so fresh results stand out. Hover over it to see when the run finished.
newBadge.where: Model row → next to the title

acceptance.title: Public acceptance layer
acceptance.description: Shade the map by the share of rural residents who support or oppose each CCUS use, from the RUB survey. Click a region to see its results, what matters most and suggestions for communication.

siteCard.title: Site card on the map
siteCard.description: Click an emitter or sink dot to see its type, location and emissions, add it to or remove it from the model, or open its details.

tour.title: Redesigned guided tour
tour.description: The tour now walks through the dashboard, map and tools step by step, with section dots and arrow-key navigation.

sinks.title: Storage and utilisation sinks
sinks.description: The node catalogue now includes storage sites and utilisation sinks with their regions and operating years.

period.title: Assessment period
period.description: Models now cover whole years. Plants are counted only for the years they operate within the assessment period.

workspaceMenu.title: Workspace menu
workspaceMenu.description: The workspace list now opens fully above the status tabs and the model list.
